newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mainly lower, early rally fizzles.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mainly lower, early rally fizzles.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures pulled back from steep early gains to finish broadly lower in volatile trading Wednesday, pressured by a late-session round of speculative profit-taking, market sources said.
Prices headed higher at the outset, defying pre-opening expectations, as speculators came in buying amid news that stevedores at Brazil's key port of Santos went on strike Wednesday.
The most-active May contract ran-up to a three-week high of 200.75 cents, but steady scale-up selling by producers and the trade capped gains and stemmed upward momentum, dealers said.
They said frustrated speculators moved to take profits after several attempts to touch off buy-stops above 200.00 cents were thwarted.

May futures closed at 193.15 cents a lb, down 1.15 cents on the day, after ranging from 200.75 to 192.00. Second-month July fell 0.90 cent, to 175.25, while the back months finished down 2.55 to up 2.70.
The May/July switch, which ballooned early in the day to around 20.00 cents, ended at 17.90 cents, down from 18.15 cents at the close on Tuesday.
The strike in Santos is scheduled to last 48 hours and could spread to national level on Friday if the dispute is not resolved, the stevedores' union said Wednesday.
Santos is Brazil's largest coffee exporting port, accounting for 984,698 60-kg bags of the 1.28 million loaded for March by March 31, according to today's Rio de Janeiro Coffee Bulletin.

While news of disruptions in the flow of coffee from top-grower Brazil compounded supply worries, traders said the Santos strike is likely to have little impact as coffee shipments traditionally slowdown at this time of the year.
"The strike does not look to be a serious situation and I'm not sure how much it will impact coffee shipments," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt. "Typically, these strikes do not last that long.
"The backround of tight nearby supplies made the reaction to the strike a little bit more than it should have been," he added.

Technically, some traders said the May contract's weak finish could spill over into Thursday. They pegged near-term support at 187.00, then 184.00. On the upside, May would still need to make a strong move through 200.00 to challenge the spot contract's life-of-contract high of 209.50.
After Wednesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were unchanged, at 83,328 60-kg bags as of April 1. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume reached an estimated 12,508 lots, up slightly from Tuesday's official tally of 11,396 lots.
